items.title: Section: What Ignorance Actually Is — Refuting the View That It Is Merely "Absent Wisdom"

items.zh: 復次，當知無明智所對治，別有心所覆蔽為性。非唯明無，亦非邪智。何以故？若彼無明唯明無者，應不可立軟中上品。由無性法，都無軟中上品異故。又不可立無明隨眠與纏差別。由無性法，於一切時其相相似，現行、隨轉不可建立。又異生心善、染、無記，於一切處常離慧明；若此無性是無明者，應一切心皆成染污。又無性法非有為攝、非無為攝；既非有為、無為所攝，不能為染，亦不為淨。
items.en: Next, it should be understood that ignorance, what genuine wisdom counters, is its own distinct mental factor, whose nature is to obscure and conceal — it is neither the mere absence of clarity, nor a distorted form of wisdom. Why? If ignorance were merely the absence of clarity, it could not be said to admit mild, middling, and intense grades, since a phenomenon without positive nature admits no such distinction of grade. Nor could latent seed and active manifestation be distinguished for it, since a phenomenon without positive nature has an identical character at all times, admitting no distinction between manifestation and latent binding. Also, since an ordinary being's mind — wholesome, defiled, or neutral — is at all times devoid of the light of undefiled wisdom, if this mere absence were ignorance, every mind whatsoever would become defiled. Also, a phenomenon without positive nature is neither conditioned nor unconditioned; being subsumed under neither, it can be neither defiled nor pure.

items.title: Section: Six Faults Close the First Refutation, and a New Rival View — Is Ignorance Simply "Wrong Wisdom"?

items.zh: 又於離明心相續中，應一切時明不得起。又不應說無明滅故，明得生起。所以者何？無有無法而可滅故。若唯邪智是無明者，為除慧明所攝諸智，餘一切智皆邪智耶？為唯染污邪執性智是邪智耶？為諸煩惱相應邪智是邪智耶？若言初智是邪智者，一切異生相續中智皆應邪智；若善、若無記，此不應道理。
items.en: Also, in a mind-continuum devoid of clarity, clarity could never arise at any time. Also, it should not be said that clarity arises because ignorance is extinguished. Why? Because there is no non-existent phenomenon that could be extinguished. If ignorance is merely wrong wisdom, does this mean: every wisdom apart from that comprising undefiled clarity is wrong wisdom? Or only defiled, wrongly grasping wisdom is wrong wisdom? Or wisdom associated with any affliction is wrong wisdom? If the first kind of wisdom is said to be wrong wisdom, then every wisdom in the continuum of an ordinary being should be wrong wisdom — yet [ordinary beings also have] wholesome and neutral [minds], which would not make sense.

items.title: Section: Why Wrong Views and Ignorance Are Not the Same, and Why Afflicted Wisdom Cannot Be Ignorance Either

items.zh: 若唯染污邪執性智是邪智者，唯應五見薩迦耶等名染性智。此中如實不了行相，是名無明。由有如實不了行故，邪執事相，是名為見。謂薩迦耶見，由無明力，執我我所；如是餘見，各於自事邪執行轉。然彼諸見不離愚癡。由癡與見行相各別，是故此五染污性智名為無明，不應道理。又若無明與諸見相無差別者，世尊不應七隨眠中，於無明外立見隨眠。又佛世尊曾無一處於諸見上示無明名。若諸煩惱相應邪智是無明者，薩迦耶等五種邪見智為自性，無二智體俱有、相應，是則諸見應與無明常不相應。又若貪等煩惱力故，令相應智成愚癡性；即應貪等增上力故，得有愚癡；非癡增上、癡為導首，故有貪等一切煩惱。又應可說：如餘煩惱相應之慧，由相應故，得成染污，非彼自性。非愚癡體可成癡性。
items.en: If only defiled, wrongly-grasping wisdom is wrong wisdom, then only the five views such as self-view should be called defiled wisdom. Here, the activity of not truly comprehending things as they are is called ignorance. Because there is this failure to truly comprehend, wrongly grasping at the characteristics of things is called view. Self-view, through the power of ignorance, grasps at "I" and "mine"; the other views likewise each wrongly grasp their own respective objects — yet none of these views are ever apart from ignorance. Because confusion and view have distinct characteristic activities, calling these five defiled wisdoms themselves "ignorance" does not make sense. Also, if ignorance and the views had no distinguishing characteristic, the Blessed One would not have established view as a separate latent tendency apart from ignorance among the seven latent tendencies. Also, the Blessed One never once, anywhere, applied the name "ignorance" to the views. If wisdom associated with any affliction is ignorance, then the five wrong views such as self-view, having wisdom as their essential nature, could never coexist with and correspond to a second instance of wisdom — so the views should never correspond with ignorance at all. Also, if the force of greed and other afflictions could turn an associated wisdom into the nature of confusion, then greed's own increasing force should itself produce confusion — and it would no longer be through confusion's increasing force, with confusion as their leader, that greed and all other afflictions come to exist. Also, it should be said that, just as wisdom associated with other afflictions becomes defiled through that very association rather than through its own essential nature, so too an essential nature that is not itself confusion cannot become the nature of confusion.

items.title: Section: The Poisoned Spring, Ignorance Confirmed as Its Own Reality, and What "Formations" Actually Means

items.zh: 又如諸餘煩惱相應，非煩惱性諸心心所。是故當知，別有無明是心所性，與心相應。如世尊言：行有三種，謂身行、語行、意行。當知此中，入出息風，名為身行。風為導首，身業轉故。身所作業，亦名身行。由愚癡者先起隨順身業風已，然後方起染污身業。如入出息能起身業，故名身行；如是尋、伺與諸語業俱名語行，受、想與意業俱名意行。如是一切總說身行、語行、意行。
items.en: Also, as with all other mental factors associated with affliction that are not themselves of the nature of affliction. Therefore it should be understood that ignorance is its own distinct mental factor, genuinely associated with mind. As the Blessed One said: formation is of three kinds — bodily formation, verbal formation, and mental formation. It should be understood that the wind of the in-breath and out-breath is called bodily formation, because wind leads the way, and bodily action follows from it. Bodily action itself is also called bodily formation, because the confused being first gives rise to the wind that accords with bodily action, and only afterwards gives rise to the defiled bodily action itself. As the in-breath and out-breath can give rise to bodily action, it is called bodily formation; likewise, examination and reflection together with verbal action are called verbal formation, and feeling and perception together with mental action are called mental formation. All of this together is called bodily formation, verbal formation, and mental formation.

items.title: Section: Birth Belongs to Whatever Realm It Falls Into, and Sorting the Twelve Links by Karma and Affliction

items.zh: 諸有隨生何界、何地，當知有支即此所攝。復次，十二支中，二業所攝，謂行及有。三煩惱攝，謂無明、愛、取。
items.en: Whatever realm or stage a being is reborn into, the existence link should be understood to be subsumed under that very realm or stage. Next, among the twelve links, two are subsumed under karmic action — formation and existence. Three are subsumed under affliction — ignorance, craving, and grasping.

items.title: Section: Drawing-Cause Versus Generating-Cause, and the Twelve Links as One Round of Cause and Effect Across Two Lives

items.zh: 當知所餘，皆事所攝。又二業中，初是引業所攝，謂行；後是生業所攝，謂有。三煩惱中，一能發起引業，謂無明；二能發起生業，謂愛、取。餘事所攝支中，二是未來苦支所攝，謂生、老死；五是未來苦因所攝。謂現法中，從行緣識，乃至觸緣受。又即五支亦是現在苦支所攝。由先世因，今得生起果異熟攝。謂識、名色、六處、觸、受。又現在果所攝五支，及未來果所攝二支，總名果所攝緣起；當知餘支，是因所攝緣起。
items.en: It should be understood that the remaining links are all subsumed under the category of event, that is, suffering. Also, of the two kinds of karmic action, the first, formation, is subsumed under the drawing-karma; the second, existence, is subsumed under the generating-karma. Of the three afflictions, one triggers the drawing-karma — ignorance; two trigger the generating-karma — craving and grasping. Among the remaining links subsumed under this category of event, two are subsumed under future suffering — birth and old age-and-death. Five are subsumed under the cause of future suffering — in the present life, from formation conditioning consciousness through contact conditioning feeling. These same five are also subsumed under present suffering, since, through a cause sown in a former life, they now arise as a ripened result — consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense-fields, contact, and feeling. Also, the five links subsumed under the present result, together with the two links subsumed under the future result, are together called the result-subsumed side of dependent origination; the remaining links should be understood as the cause-subsumed side of dependent origination.

blocks.text: Is ignorance just the absence of wisdom? Or wrong wisdom? The treatise argues it is neither: it is a real mental factor of its own, whose nature is obscuring.
"Ignorance, which wisdom counters, is its own distinct mental factor with obscuring as its nature." If it were a mere absence, it could not have grades, nor exist as seed and manifestation.

Ordinary minds always lack clarity; if lack of clarity were ignorance, every ordinary mind would be defiled, yet good and neutral minds exist. Master Cháng Bǎi: if wrong wisdom were ignorance, which wrong wisdom would it be?

"Not truly comprehending is ignorance; because of it, wrongly grasping the marks of things is view." Master Cháng Bǎi: view has ignorance and adds wrong grasping. The Buddha lists view as a latent tendency apart from ignorance.
The wind of breath is bodily formation, since wind leads and bodily action follows.
Whatever realm a being is reborn into, the link of existence belongs to it.
Formations and existence are karma; ignorance, craving, and grasping are affliction; the rest are result. Ignorance triggers drawing karma; craving and grasping trigger generating karma.
Ignorance as "obscuring" is a helpful image: not a lack, but a cover. A cover can be removed.

quiz.q: What does the treatise hold ignorance to be and not to be?
options: simply lacking wisdom, with no nature of its own, as dark is no light, ignorance being clarity's absence
simply wrong wisdom, corrupted wisdom being ignorance
a distinct mental factor whose nature is to obscure; neither mere absence of clarity nor wrong wisdom
simply craving
quiz.why: The treatise says ignorance, which wisdom counters, is its own distinct mental factor with obscuring as its nature, neither the mere absence of clarity nor wrong wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: its character is to obscure, covering our mind and giving rise to delusion. Two rival views are refuted in the following sections.

quiz.q: If ignorance were merely absence of clarity, what is the first fault?
options: ignorance would be joined with craving, the unwise all craving, so ignorance and craving would be one
clarity could not arise
no mild, middling, and intense grades could be set, a phenomenon without nature having no such difference
buddhas too would have ignorance
quiz.why: The treatise's first argument: were ignorance a mere absence, there could be no grades, since a phenomenon without nature has no such difference. Master Cháng Bǎi: without real substance, differences of grade cannot be spoken of; yet formless beings have soft ignorance, form-realm beings medium, and desire-realm beings superior.

quiz.q: If ignorance were mere absence, why could latent seed and manifestation not be distinguished?
options: because latent seed and manifestation are one thing, separated only for convenience, so the objection fails
a phenomenon without nature has one appearance at all times, so seed and manifestation cannot be set up
because ordinary beings have no latent seeds
because noble ones have no manifestation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a phenomenon without nature has the same appearance at all times, and so seed and manifestation cannot be established. Ignorance demonstrably does have both, latent and active, and so it cannot be a mere lack. The same argument form runs through the following faults.

quiz.q: If ignorance were mere absence, what of ordinary beings' good minds, and why could one not say clarity arises as ignorance ends?
options: ordinary minds always lack that clarity, so all would be defiled; and no non-existent thing can be extinguished
ordinary good minds would become noble ones' uncontaminated minds; ignorance is real and ends so clarity arises, as the treatise agrees
ordinary beings would have no mind; clarity would never arise
ordinary beings would be arhats; ignorance need not end
quiz.why: The treatise argues that ordinary minds always lack clarity, so every mind would be defiled, though good and neutral minds exist; and that one could not say clarity arises as ignorance ends, there being nothing non-existent to extinguish. Master Cháng Bǎi: a phenomenon without nature has no arising or ceasing. The English uses two renderings for 慧明.

quiz.q: If wrong wisdom is ignorance, which three are asked about, and why does the first fail?
options: wisdom of hearing, reflection, and cultivation; the first makes all hearing wrong, which is plainly false
dharma, subsequent, and worldly knowledge; the first makes dharma-knowledge wrong
all wisdom but clarity, defiled grasping wisdom, wisdom joined with affliction; the first makes all ordinary wisdom wrong, yet they have good and neutral minds
superior, middling, and inferior wisdom; the first makes superior wisdom wrong
quiz.why: The treatise asks which is meant: all wisdom apart from clarity, only defiled grasping wisdom, or wisdom joined with affliction. Master Cháng Bǎi: if wrong wisdom is ignorance, which wrong wisdom is it? In fact ordinary beings sometimes have good and neutral states, so the first cannot stand. The other two are taken up in §56.

quiz.q: How do ignorance and view differ, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: ignorance is wrong grasping and view is failure to comprehend, view coming first as the cause of ignorance
they are exactly the same
ignorance is form and view mental
failing to truly comprehend is ignorance; wrongly grasping from this is view; view has ignorance plus wrong grasping
quiz.why: The treatise says not truly comprehending is ignorance; because of it, wrongly grasping the marks of things is view. Master Cháng Bǎi: view and ignorance differ; view has ignorance and adds wrong grasping. The two differ in aspect, so the five defiled wisdoms cannot themselves be ignorance.

quiz.q: What scriptural evidence shows ignorance and view differ?
options: among seven latent tendencies view is set apart from ignorance; the Buddha never gave views the name ignorance
among the four truths ignorance is suffering and view origin, the plainest evidence being two truths
view is the first of the twelve links
among the five hindrances, each is one
quiz.why: The treatise argues from scripture: the Blessed One lists view as a latent tendency apart from ignorance, and nowhere gives views the name ignorance. Master Cháng Bǎi: among the seven latent tendencies, ignorance and view are two. So teaching and reasoning agree.

quiz.q: The English has "comprehending the characteristic activity of things" for 如實不了行相. Whose is 行相?
options: 行相 belongs to outer things, their activity, so the English is exact, ignorance not knowing how things work
行相 means practice
行相 means the formations aggregate
行相 belongs to ignorance itself, whose mode is not comprehending; the English makes it the mode of things not comprehended
quiz.why: The Chinese pairs two clauses: not comprehending truly is ignorance's mode of operation, and wrongly grasping the marks of things is view. The first 行相 thus belongs to ignorance. Master Cháng Bǎi: view is grasping that comes from not understanding the facts. The English, rendering it "of things," blurs the contrast of mode and object.

quiz.q: Why could views not be joined with ignorance if it were wisdom joined with affliction?
options: because views are wholesome, unable to join affliction, so ignorance and view never join, as the treatise means
because views are form
because only noble ones have views
the five views have wisdom as their nature, and no two wisdoms can coexist
quiz.why: The treatise reasons that the five views have wisdom as their nature, and two instances of the factor cannot coexist, so views could never be joined with ignorance if it too were wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: two factors of wisdom cannot appear together. Yet views are always accompanied by ignorance, so ignorance must be a separate factor.

quiz.q: What are bodily, verbal, and mental formations, and why is breath called bodily formation?
options: breath and bodily action; investigation and verbal action; feeling, perception, and mental action; wind leads, the wind according with action arising before defiled action
bodily formation is walking, verbal is reciting, mental is meditating, three practices unrelated to wind
all three mean only karmic seeds
all three mean only ignorance
quiz.why: The treatise says the wind of breath is bodily formation, since wind leads and bodily action follows. Master Cháng Bǎi: wind's nature is lightness and movement, and the body can move because wind moves within; deluded beings first give rise to wind according with bodily action, then create defiled action. Investigation and verbal action, and feeling, perception, and mental action, are the others.

quiz.q: To which realm or stage does the existence link belong, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: it always belongs to the desire realm, karma being made there, so higher beings lack their own
it belongs to whatever realm one is reborn into; for rebirth in the form realm it is form existence
it belongs to no realm
it belongs to all three at once
quiz.why: The treatise says that whatever realm or stage a being is reborn into, the existence link belongs to it. Master Cháng Bǎi: if the next life is in the form realm, the existence link is form existence; since it is closest to the coming rebirth, it belongs to that stage. Thus the seeds moistened by craving take the name of the coming realm.

quiz.q: How are the twelve links divided among karma, affliction, and result?
options: ignorance and craving under karma; formations, existence, grasping under affliction; the other seven under result
all twelve under karma
formations and existence under karma; ignorance, craving, grasping under affliction; the other seven under result
all twelve under affliction
quiz.why: The treatise assigns formations and existence to karma; ignorance, craving, and grasping to affliction; and the rest to 事, result. Master Cháng Bǎi says each of the three is an affliction. The English overview's "drawing" and "generating" rounds should keep to this: ignorance raises drawing karma, and craving and grasping generating karma.

quiz.q: The English has "the category of suffering" for 事所攝. Why, and with what gain and loss?
options: 事 has nothing to do with suffering, meaning worldly affairs, so "suffering" is wrong
the lecture says 事 is the ripened result of suffering, also called subsumed under suffering, so the English keeps the sense but loses the word
事 means occupation
事 means matters of practice
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 事 is the ripened result of suffering, and being subsumed under it is also called subsumed under suffering. So the English is justified in sense, and the usual triad of affliction, karma, and suffering stands behind it. Yet the treatise's own term is 事, and a reader comparing the texts should know this.

quiz.q: Which afflictions trigger drawing-karma and generating-karma?
options: craving and grasping trigger drawing-karma; ignorance triggers generating-karma, being last to moisten rebirth
ignorance triggers drawing-karma, formation; craving and grasping trigger generating-karma, existence
all three trigger only drawing-karma
none of the three triggers karma
quiz.why: The treatise says ignorance triggers drawing-karma and craving and grasping trigger generating-karma. Master Cháng Bǎi: the ignorance link draws forth the next life's result; the drawing and drawn are the drawing cause, the generating links are the generating cause, and only birth and ageing-death are result. So these are not two separate rounds of lives.
